topics.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are each cutting their own chip deals to escape Nvidia's queue
topics.why: Anthropic is reportedly in talks with Samsung on a custom AI chip and OpenAI has detailed Jalapeno, its Broadcom-built inference ASIC -- the frontier labs are starting to build around the hardware bottleneck instead of just paying for more of it.

topics.title: ChatGPT Search just hit a fifth of Google's volume, and publishers want paying for it
topics.why: OpenAI says ChatGPT Search has reached one-fifth of Google's search volume, and publishers are now arguing AI answers that replace articles outright should come with compensation -- the search/media fight is no longer hypothetical.

topics.title: A dozen governments just signed a Paris pact on AI safety -- while the US sat it out
topics.why: The French Presidency's Paris Call for AI Safety and Security landed November 9, a fresh attempt at international coordination right as the US keeps betting on a lighter-touch, compute-first strategy.

topics.title: China is targeting 80% domestic chips for its next AI buildout -- and Meta just picked a side
topics.why: A draft plan reportedly pushes China toward chip self-sufficiency for a $295B data-center push, while Meta's return to open-weight models is explicitly framed as out-competing China on openness -- the AI race is splitting into two supply chains.

topics.title: A new benchmark just showed how shaky 'agentic' claims really are
topics.why: SemiAnalysis's new GDPx benchmark tests frontier models on real agentic tasks rather than static Q&A -- a timely check on the gap between vendor demos and what AI agents can actually finish unsupervised, right as eval and red-teaming work becomes its own career lane.
